REFERRED TO CORPORATIONS, AUTHORITIES AND COMMISSIONS

items.lawSection: Port Authority of New York and New Jersey
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S3921

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend chapter 154 of the laws of 1921 constituting the Port
of New York Authority, in relation to reform of such authority


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA :

To enact the Port Authority Reform Act of 2007.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Section 1, Short Title.

§ 2. Legislative Findings; Board of Commissioner Reform The Board of
Commissioner Reform includes an adoption of a code of ethics,
establishment of written policies, creating a statutory fiduciary
responsibility, as well as audit and governance committees.

§§ 3 and 4. Reforms the Open Meetings Requirements, Liberalize the
Open Meetings Requirements and require conformity to the Open Meetings
Laws of New York & New Jersey.

§ 5 A. Disposition of Property (new section 1-c). This section
establishes rules for the disposition of Port Authority property.

B. Independent Inspector General (new section 1-d). This section will
create an independent inspector general.

C. Independent Budget Office (new section 1-e). This section will
create an independent budget office.

D. Debt Reform (new section 1-f). This section will reform the process
for issuing debt.

E. Procurement Reform (new section 1-g). This section would establish
rules and set limits on procurement contracts and lobbying.

§ 6. Enacting Clause

 JUSTIFICATION :

This legislation will extend recent reform measures (see Chapter 766
of the Laws of 2005) enacted affecting New York-only public
authorities to the Port Authority of New York & New Jersey

As a bi-state authority, identical legislation affecting the Port
Authority must be enacted by both New York and New Jersey. The
committees on Corporations, Authorities and Commissions in each house
of New York Legislature has worked closely and cooperatively with the
New Jersey Legislature which has yielded identical legislation (see
New Jersey Senate Bill 2358; Senator Ellen Karcher).

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2007: Senate Corporations, Authorities and Commissions Cmte./ Assembly
Corporations, Authorities and Commissions Cmte.
2008: Passed Senate/Assembly Codes Cmte.

 FISCAL IMPLICATION FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS :

None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect upon the enactment into law by the state of
New Jersey of legislation having an identical effect with this act,
but if the state of New Jersey shall have already enacted such
legislation, this act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Establishes a substantive reform policy regarding the New York and New Jersey port authority; creates several new positions, including a port authority inspector general, a port authority independent budget officer, and an independent central procurement officer; relates to how the port authority may dispose of its property.
title: Establishes a substantive reform policy regarding the New York and New Jersey port authority
